one_star_reviews.text:
⭐ 1-star review

We went to view Monkey Puzzle Walton-on-Thames for our toddler, and unfortunately the experience was very disappointing.

When we initially filled in the application form, we mentioned that we were looking for half-day sessions, but we never received an answer about this. I contacted the nursery three times by phone without getting a clear response, and my mother-in-law then had to contact them twice. Eventually, we were told to ask me to call them, so we arranged to go and view the nursery.

During the viewing, we were told that they would not accept children attending only on their government-funded hours and would not offer half-day sessions. We were told that we would have to do at least two full days, from 7:30am to 6:30pm, otherwise they would not accept our child.

The manager also told us that no other nursery in the area would offer half-day sessions because “that’s how it works there.” We have since found out that this is not true, as other nurseries do offer half-day arrangements.

Afterwards, when I mentioned our experience to two of my clients, they independently told me that they had experienced the same thing when they went to view the nursery for their own children.

I completely understand that a nursery can choose which sessions it offers, but I found the way this was handled very disappointing.

Based on our experience, we decided that Monkey Puzzle Walton-on-Thames was not the right nursery for our child.

one_star_reviews.text:
I purchased three Boston Ferns from Aussie Care Pro for approximately $200, and I am genuinely shocked by what arrived.
The plants I received looked nothing like the lush, healthy ferns advertised on the website. The quality was extremely poor, and in my opinion they looked like they were worth only a few dollars each. They were sparse, unimpressive, and nowhere near what I expected based on the product photos and description.
I contacted customer service to raise my concerns and sought a reasonable resolution. Rather than accepting responsibility for supplying products that were significantly different from what was advertised, I was repeatedly told that I would have to pay return shipping costs if I wanted a full refund. After multiple emails, their position never changed.

My experience with this service has been nothing short of catastrophic. Their systems are disorganised and ineffective, leaving me feeling that my care is utterly unimportant. Issues are never resolved, they simply do not listen, do not act, and do not fix complaints.

They even lost my assessment on the waiting list, so I had to chase just to be seen for that. I have been waiting thirteen months for titration with no resolution in sight, and now, after spending over twelve hours trying to contact them, I am still unheard. Their chat system is glitchy, I was blocked from talking to an agent (it kept telling me it wasn't available during their working hours) so I tried calling them. After waiting over two hours, my call is still unanswered past their closing time. This is not an isolated incident and happens repeatedly.

They have also not acknowledged my complaint.

The combination of unresponsiveness, poor systems, and dismissive treatment makes this service intolerable. I deeply regret being referred here. I don't understand how they got a Good rating with the CQC because my care from start to finish has been inadequate.

It gets worse, after chasing for 6 months because I was led to believe I didn't have another choice they titrated me on a very high dose of a medication that had side effects that ultimately meant I couldn't take them for my own health and now I've got nothing.

They also ignored my complaints so I haven't been able to complain to the Ombudsman.

Just stay away for your own sanity. I really don't know how I'm getting out of this. It was supposed to support, but their systems mean they can fail in their duty of care without any accountability.

Waited over a year for titration just for it to be done with in 12 weeks and didn’t even have a doctor for half the time (multiple times asked what happened and no one can tell me why) PTUK do do not care about or listen to patients. The service is appalling and basically committing fraud but taking Gods knows how many millions of NHS money and providing a substandard level of care.

Absolutely disgusting. DO NOT GO TO THESE IF YOU HAVE RIGHT TO CHOOSE!!!! They advertised waiting times that would have had me assessed in November 2025 and told me on live chat that I would be assessed in Nov 2025.

It's now September 2026 and they have just offered me an assessment appointment for MARCH 2027. It actually would have been quicker to go through the NHS instead of right to choose. They lie about timelines to get as many patients on their books as they can to bleed money from the NHS and then leave you hanging forever without any respect or consideration for how it impacts you. I am now pursuing legal action.

*edit - I successfully transferred to a different provider for titration only and was given an appointment within 3 weeks. I wish I had done it much sooner. Something is going seriously wrong at Psychiatry UK for this to be happening. I’ve seen they recently updated their titration wait time to 14-15 months which is so unacceptable. This includes for people who have already been on the list for over a year. They state they are ‘working hard’ to reduce this but I have only ever seen it increase.
If you are still waiting to start meds with them please look into transferring to a different provider. Some of them you do not need to be re-assessed, you can just provide your existing diagnosis report.

Please avoid this service especially if you are right to choose. You shouldn’t have to wait a year to begin the treatment you need. The lack of care is astounding. Please research other right to choose providers as they have much shorter wait times, do not accept being referred here. My mental health is the worst it ever has been and they don’t listen despite repeated contact from my GP. I am off sick from work for almost 2 months and they still refuse to help me.

I wish I could give 0 stars. The standard of care I have received from Psychiatry UK has been appalling.

I requested a repeat prescription on 4 August 2026. Despite this being medication prescribed as part of my medical care, my request went unanswered for an entire month.

I eventually received a call from my prescriber, Sunny Aujla, who told me that he had been on holiday and had subsequently been unable to log into the system, which was why he had not responded. In my view, leaving a patient without a response to a prescription request for a month because of annual leave and IT access issues is completely unacceptable. A healthcare provider should have systems in place to ensure continuity of care when an individual member of staff is unavailable.

I was then assured that my prescription would be fast-tracked and sent to me.

It wasn't.

Instead, I was left waiting yet again. I sent multiple notes asking for updates and, once again, received no response.

Today, nearly two months after my original request, my medication finally arrived. I opened the parcel only to discover that just half of my medication had been supplied.

So after weeks of chasing, repeated unanswered messages, an assurance that my prescription would be fast-tracked, and nearly two months of waiting, Psychiatry UK still failed to provide my complete prescription.

For a healthcare provider dealing with psychiatric medication, I find this level of communication and continuity of care deeply concerning. Patients should not have to repeatedly chase a medical provider simply to receive prescribed medication, nor should they be left wondering for weeks whether anybody is even dealing with their request.

This experience has taken a significant physical, mental and emotional toll on me. What makes it worse is how utterly avoidable it feels. Staff holidays, IT problems and internal communication failures should not become a patient's medical problem.

I am posting this because I genuinely hope Psychiatry UK takes responsibility for what happened and addresses whatever failures allowed it to happen. More importantly, I hope prospective patients understand the experience I have had before entrusting this service with their care.

Nearly two months to fulfil a repeat prescription, only for half of it to arrive, is simply unacceptable.

I was quite shocked that James sent me this link to rate his practice but it sort of  sums up the ego of the man.
I wouldn't normally comment on something in the negative because of the loss of income it may have.
I think I am still struggling with PTSD because of the treatment I received at James's fumbling hands. I often felt assaulted after leaving his chair and it took me hours to understand what had occurred.
My wife would say don't go back but you pay in advance and how can you get another dentist to continue the work.
I had a crown and 2 porcelain inserts.
He used so much force pushing the Crown on to the tooth ,( 2 fingers on top of the crown and 2 thumbs under my chin) that the bottom of the crown shattered and broke off a few days latter. He did offer to replace the whole thing but I couldn't let him abuse my poor tooth further.
One of the inserts didn't fit so he reduced my tooth to nothing to make it fit . That appointment was supposed to take 30mins with no drilling and no injections . I had arranged to meet friends for lunch and after 2hrs hours of drilling and 4 injections I was to traumatized to meet anyone..
James has zero empathy and zero communication skills. He doesn't explain what he is doing when things go wrong. The porcelain inserts could have been an ordinary filling but he promised I would never need another filling if I had the insert. They come with a 4 yr guarantee but I will never claim on that as I would sooner loose the tooth than sit in his chair again. The gum around that tooth still causes pain every day and is sensitive to hot and cold ,  I will rebuild my confidence hopefully enough to see another dentist.
On the upside I now clean my teeth twice a day and use interdental brushes in the hope I will never have to suffer the same traumatic experience again.
So to summarise from my experience I would say.
James has very poor communication skills
James has limited manual dexterity
And he has has very little empathy
I don't think he ever kept an appointment , always changing the time on the day of the appointment and he is stunningly expensive.

one_star_reviews.text:
I was extremely disappointed with the advice I received following an enquiry about a small lump on my eyelid after blepharoplasty.

After reviewing a photograph, I was told that it appeared to be a nodule within the blepharoplasty scar and that it would likely require a unilateral revision blepharoplasty, with an estimated cost of £1,250. I was also advised that an initial consultation would cost £250.

Naturally, this caused me unnecessary concern, particularly as it suggested I might need further surgery.

I subsequently went back to my original surgeon, who identified the issue as a milia and resolved it in approximately 10 seconds, completely free of charge. No revision surgery was needed.

I appreciate that it can be difficult to make a definitive diagnosis from a photograph alone, but I feel that recommending potentially unnecessary surgery and quoting such a significant cost without an in-person examination was premature and unnecessarily alarming.

This experience has seriously undermined my confidence in the advice I was given. I would encourage anyone in a similar situation to seek a second opinion before committing to expensive consultations or further surgery.

I am writing this review as a desperate mother to urge other parents to exercise extreme caution if considering Sasha Hvidsten Ltd for a child or teenager struggling with severe mental health issues.
We brought our 13-year-old daughter to this clinic in desperate need of urgent, professional mental health support. She was initially seen and diagnosed by Dr. Saeed Nazir. For a £600 consultation, we received a superficial report that completely failed to reflect the severity and nuance of her condition, dismissing her complex issues as basic depression. He prescribed a medication known to carry side effects that can increase suicidal ideation—an issue she was already struggling with—without offering adequate follow-up plans, continuous monitoring, or clear lines of communication. Shortly after, Dr. Nazir left the clinic.
We were then seen by Dr. Syed Mehdi for a follow-up. In our experience, he completely failed to appreciate her true state of mind, brushing off her situation with dismissive comments and failing to recognize the risks associated with her medication. Despite her high-risk state, he expressed satisfaction with her condition and issued a further 4-month prescription without proper safeguards or close oversight.
Tragically, in August, our daughter attempted suicide.
Throughout this entire process, we felt this clinic acted purely as a business rather than a compassionate, responsible care provider. There was no real duty of care, no proper risk monitoring, and a total failure to recognize masking or critical warning signs. All we received for our money was a superficial report, risky prescriptions, and no meaningful ongoing support.
Parents seeking serious, life-saving help for their vulnerable teenagers deserve thorough, safe, and attentive medical care. In our experience, this clinic did not provide that. I would strongly advise parents to look elsewhere for genuine professional support.

one_star_reviews.text: Used this company for my mothers funeral and I was so saddened by the way we as a family were treated, we used a lady called Julie before for my dads funeral and couldn’t have been happier. When we made the arrangements with Orlando he seemed very dismissive of our last experience with Julie and told us she had moved away and was no longer part of the organisation, so we reluctantly used another celebrant who was very good. Unfortunately Orlando failed to keep us informed of any updates and we had to chase him for clarification on donations as we hadn’t received any form of confirmation about them reaching our chosen charity. Orlando never responded to our calls or messages and we eventually called the charity who said they hadn’t received anything from Oak funeral services on behalf of mum. As you can imagine this was very distressing, after giving Orlando and ultimatum we eventually got confirmation of the donations received, but if I’m honest I don’t have any confidence it’s correct. I found out 3 weeks after the service that Julie was still employed by Oak funeral service and hadn’t moved away, this made our whole family upset as we felt we had been lied to. If a funeral director can lie about this what else are they hiding because they certainly didn’t deal With the donations in an honest manner. I have oils use these funeral services again. They have lost my trust and respect.

Wish it could be 0 stars. The only 1 star is for the reception staff, who are at least polite. Even standing outside on the street, you can constantly hear screaming and crying echoing from the unit. Walking inside, the environment is profoundly distressing, and it is painfully obvious that patients are actively declining mentally due to sheer negligence, something I know firsthand from witnessing it with my own eyes, hearing it happen while on the phone, and being told it directly by my loved one who is sadly stuck on that unit.

​The culture among staff is dismissive, punitive, and entirely devoid of empathy. Basic confidentiality and trust are routinely breached, leaving patients with no safe way to voice concerns or seek outside help without facing blowback. Concerns raised by loved ones are brushed aside, and families are kept at arm's length by rigid, consultant-dictated visiting restrictions that cut vulnerable patients off from their support systems when they need them most. To make matters worse, staff actively weaponize family involvement—even using loved ones as leverage or "bait" to enforce compliance, rather than prioritizing the patient's well-being.

​Treatment here is completely counterproductive. Staff are entirely unequipped to provide proper meal support, and instead of helping patients through meals, they resort to victim-blaming—telling individuals fighting severe eating disorders that they "only have themselves to blame" when interventions like nasogastric tubes become necessary. When NG feeds are forced, staff rely on heavy-handed, aggressive physical restraints performed incorrectly, frequently leaving patients bruised and physically harmed. To make matters worse, staff fail so completely in their duties that vulnerable patients are left to support and comfort each other through their breakdowns—an entirely unacceptable dynamic when everyone there is intensely unwell and fighting their own battles. Weight management is weaponized as a tool for punishment rather than part of a holistic recovery framework, completely ignoring the psychological reality of the illness.

​This place is entirely unfit for purpose and needs to be shut down immediately. If you or anyone you care about is fighting an eating disorder, do not send them to Ellern Mede Barnet. These individuals deserve a facility focused on actual safety and mental healthcare, not a toxic system that punishes patients for being ill.

Given the value of the installation, the quality concerns and the difficulty obtaining basic technical information, my experience to date has been extremely disappointing.

one_star_reviews.text:
My son attended this nursery for one year, having previously spent three years at a different nursery. We chose to move him for his final year before starting school because we wanted a term-time-only nursery. Unfortunately, our experience was very mixed, and there are several things I feel other parents should be aware of before making their decision.

One of my biggest concerns was the lack of communication. Emails to the manager regarding enquiries or concerns could take a week or sometimes longer to receive a response. On several occasions, when a response eventually came, the original question had not actually been addressed, resulting in lengthy back-and-forth communication. Eventually, I often found it easier to call.

There were also multiple changes of key workers within just a few months, which had a noticeable impact on my son. He became upset and unsettled after losing staff members he had built strong relationships with. I would like to give special thanks to Mispa and Bahar, who were absolutely wonderful with my son when he first started. They understood him, supported him, encouraged him and challenged him to do more. Unfortunately, after they left, our experience was not the same.

I also had concerns about learning and school readiness. I did not feel there was enough focus on progressing my son academically or preparing him for starting school. He often spent significant amounts of time with the younger children doing activities such as colouring, which did not always challenge or stimulate him at the level I felt was appropriate for his age. He would sometimes come home saying he was bored.

I had to repeatedly request information about his learning and development, and it took months before I received a report. When I eventually received it, I did not feel that it accurately reflected his level or the progress I had observed. As a parent, this was particularly disappointing because I expected regular and meaningful communication about his development throughout the year.

I also felt there were limited extracurricular activities and opportunities to keep the children engaged and provide additional experiences outside of their usual routine.

In terms of safeguarding and supervision, there were situations during the year that left me with concerns and questioning whether the nursery was always providing the level of care and oversight I would expect for my child. This is something every parent should consider carefully when choosing a nursery.

I am grateful to the staff members who genuinely cared for my son, particularly Mispa and Bahar, and I know there are individuals within the nursery who work hard. However, as a parent, I have to be honest about our overall experience.

Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this nursery to other parents based on our experience. I would strongly encourage anyone considering it to do thorough research, ask questions about staff turnover, communication, learning and development, school readiness, and safeguarding, and take the time to make sure it is the right environment for their child.

I sincerely hope that the feedback from parents is taken on board and that improvements are made for the children and families who attend in the future.

one_star_reviews.text: Based on our experience with Drive Espana before, during and after our recent 1-week classic car tour thru Andalusia in Sept 2026 (Denia, Lorca, Granada, Cordoba, Cuenca, El Saler, Denia) we will definitively look for other agencies when planning future tours. The service Drive Espana provided for our group did not meet a single criteria relevant to our group. Missing quality and consideration regarding proposed routes, stops, group meals. In addition we experienced customer orientation in the most adverse form when addressing these shortcomings. In hindsight we should have checked available online comments and previous customer feedback in more detail. See ChatGPT, Grok, Claude indicating that the few reviews regarding the marketed experience (>120 tours organised) mostly appear on Drive Espana's website. In our case the Drive Espana physical Roadblock arrived last minute making it difficult to better prepare in due time. When we then raised concerns regarding the non-scenic, busy, routes proposed in the roadbook, Drive Espana's owner responded: "Book is adequate because nobody has yet failed to find a hotel and that is the measure of whether or not the road is adequate." This summarises the diametral differences in expectations very well. In our opinion scenic routes and quality stops should be the core value and experience of a company offering specialty services for classic car tours. Based on a claim of 120+ tours organised one would expect a solid standing with hotels and their services, too. We could not experience that. The opposite was true: failing arrangements (several hotel dinners / parking) and no sense of a welcome back as a tour / group organised by Drive Espana. Luckily we are a group of people that were able enjoy our time together - not because of Drive Espana, but despite of the service we experienced from this agency.

In September, we took part in an eight-day classic car tour through Andalusia organised by Drive España. Our group consisted of a great selection of classic cars, including an Austin-Healey, AC Cobra, Jaguar E-Type, MGAs, Mercedes SLs, Porsches and others.

Speaking on behalf of several participants, unfortunately, we felt that the service provided by Drive España fell short of what we would expect from an organiser specialising in classic car tours.

A number of the routes were not particularly suitable for vintage and classic cars. Lunch stops were not properly planned, and the organised group dinners generally did not meet our expectations in terms of either food quality or location.

More generally, the event often felt as though it lacked the care, attention to detail and personal touch that you would expect from a professionally organised classic car tour. At several of the hotels, the group did not appear to have been properly prepared for, and in some cases even parking arrangements had not been organised in advance.

Several participants raised these concerns directly with the owner of Drive España. Unfortunately, rather than taking responsibility for the shortcomings or addressing the feedback constructively, he attributed many of the problems to members of our club and to the hotels.

Overall, our experience was disappointing. Drive España appears to have received a number of very positive reviews, but based on our experience, we unfortunately cannot share that assessment. For a classic car tour, we would expect considerably more attention to detail, better planning and a stronger focus on the specific needs of classic car drivers.

I feel compelled to leave this review now I am finally pregnant through an alternative IVF clinic and have had a polar opposite experience to what I had with IVF London. I had multiple awful experiences with IVF London, initially via Apricity (2 x ERs & 2 x FETs) and then as a direct client (1 x FET).

They seemed to have high staff turnover, and the ones who seemed compassionate left after my first FET.

I had a blighted ovum on my 2nd FET which I found out at my 6 week scan. The doctor who scanned me told me not to cry like I was being silly, questioned my dates like I’d got the timings incorrect and then proceeded to leave the room and not communicate any further leaving me sobbing with the nurses. I had to come back a few days later for a blood test to confirm the pregnancy was concluding and they kept me waiting in reception for 45 minutes crying whilst every member of staff cooed over another client’s baby right infront of me. Finally a kind nurse noticed and pulled me away apologising for the terrible conduct and lack of empathy.

On my third FET, the doctor informed me one of my embryos never thawed correctly whilst I was naked on the bed about to have the transfer. He then tried to pressure me and my husband into add ons for our one remaining embryo whilst we were in shock (and I was still undressed). Needless to say, that FET failed.

I would also like to add that I believe they are misusing Google reviews - on the phone the receptionist said to me they would give me a free consultation with the doctor if I left a 5 star review.

I would highly recommend looking elsewhere for treatment, and now I’ve seen what good looks like, I am even more gutted by what I experienced here.

Ps. To the clinic, if you try to say you can’t find me on your database like you have with other comments on here, I will email you directly to confirm. Based on the nature of my case you should be able to work out who I am.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointing experience from start to finish.

We booked a 2pm appointment specifically to view two vehicles. We arrived at 1:55pm and were approached by a member of staff who asked if I was there to sell my vehicle. After explaining that we had an appointment, we were told that the first car we had come to view was actually at their other site and still needed to be washed.

We were told it would be 10 minutes maximum, but it took nearly 40 minutes before the car eventually arrived.

While we were waiting, there was a Porsche Macan for sale at the premises. We witnessed a member of staff get into it and drive away extremely aggressively, "like he'd stolen it" would be the best way to describe it. Seeing a vehicle being driven like that when it was apparently stock for sale certainly wasn't reassuring as a prospective customer.

When the vehicle we'd booked to see eventually arrived, it was disappointing. It was still dirty and had numerous scratches, stone chips and visible polishing/buffing marks across the paintwork. It certainly wasn't presented to the standard I would expect for a pre-arranged viewing, particularly when we'd travelled there genuinely considering purchasing it.

More concerningly, there was also a loud knocking noise from the air suspension when it was being operated. I can't say what was causing it, but it was certainly noticeable and did nothing to inspire confidence in the vehicle.

We had also specifically told the lady on the phone that we were travelling down to view two X5s. When we asked about the second one, we were initially told it was a customer's car and they didn't currently have it. We were then told that each salesman manages and sells their own stock and that another salesman was responsible for that particular X5, so we would need to deal with him. The explanation then appeared to change again, and we were told the vehicle was actually at their other location.

Once we made it clear that we still wanted to view the other X5 and potentially speak with the salesman responsible for it, the salesman dealing with us appeared to completely lose interest. At one point, he sat in the driver's seat of the X5 we were considering purchasing and started texting on his phone while we were trying to inspect the vehicle. It came across as incredibly unprofessional.

The showroom itself wasn't particularly pleasant either. There was a strong smell of pizza throughout, and one of the offices appeared to have effectively become a room where employees were eating/storing pizza. Again, it didn't create a particularly professional environment when you're visiting a dealership potentially looking to spend a significant amount of money.

We arrived with a genuine intention of potentially purchasing one of two vehicles. Instead, we experienced a long wait despite having an appointment, conflicting explanations about the second vehicle, poor presentation of the car we did see, a concerning noise from its suspension, and a general lack of professionalism.

We ended the appointment by walking away whilst the salesman was still sat in the driver's seat of the vehicle on his phone. No acknowledgement, nothing.

Based entirely on our experience, I would not recommend Reverie Autos and certainly wouldn't make another journey there to view a vehicle.

**Avoid Tiny Explorers at All Costs – A Dreadful Business Powered by Horrific Customer Service**

On paper, Tiny Explorers sounds like a fantastic concept. A service offering to ease the burden of travelling with young children by supplying essential gear for holidaying parents is a brilliant, much-needed idea. In practice, however, dealing with this company was hands-down the worst customer service experience I have ever had.

Our experience began with our order arriving with some items ordered completely missing. To make matters worse, the main item that *did* manage to arrive was incomplete and not as advertised on their website.

Hoping to resolve the issue reasonably, I contacted their team and gave them every opportunity to rectify their mistakes. Instead of taking ownership, their customer service correspondence was astonishingly rude, deeply condescending, slow, and utterly unhelpful. They showed zero interest in making things right for a customer left in a lurch whilst trying to enjoy a holiday.

It comes as no surprise to learn that the owner is currently looking to sell the business. Judging by the sheer volume of identical reviews online, my experience is far from unique; it is simply how this company operates.

Tiny Explorers is entirely not worth the hassle, stress, or money. Save yourself the headache and take your custom to a reliable competitor instead.

Wouldn’t recommend and wouldn’t go again. Took my 2 year old for the first time yesterday - my partner unexpectedly ended up coming. He wasn’t on the booking - I thought it would be okay for him to pay when we got there. They had him stand and wait at the entrance for 10 minutes as they had a “problem with the tills”.  They then told him they were at full capacity and he wasn’t allowed in and he had to leave. I could understand if we turned up with extra children but it was one extra adult who would’ve been sat on the table. There is no phone signal up there so I couldn’t contact anyone - I asked for their WiFi and was told it was “only for the tills” and to try and log in to Toolstations WiFi next door but that it will drop depending on where I am in the room. It was incredibly hard to connect to and it wouldn’t stay connected.

I bought snacks with me for my toddler - the staff saw his lunch box. I was told he couldn’t eat any food from home there. There’s lots of signs there saying you will be asked to leave and banned. I think this is ridiculous- especially for fussy eaters or those with allergies. The food they had was tiny portions and massively overpriced. All very processed and full of sugar too so not great for health conscious parents. I had already paid £11 to get in so I thought this was very cheeky.

I couldn’t get myself a drink as my partner left with his wallet and my purse was in the car.

There was feral unsupervised older children running everywhere and they knocked my son over twice within the first 30 minutes of him playing. No idea where their parents were. If I wasn’t waiting for my friend I would’ve left straight away.

Wouldn’t recommend, will never be going back. I’ve not heard anything good about the nursery either.

one_star_reviews.text:
I had a very disappointing experience with Clinical Partners when I underwent an assessment for autism.

I went into the assessment expecting a thorough, objective assessment of my lifelong experiences and difficulties. Unfortunately, I came away feeling that I had not been properly heard or that the full picture of my developmental history had been adequately considered.

One of my main concerns was the information available about my childhood. My parents are both deceased, so obtaining reliable childhood evidence was already difficult. The informant used as part of my assessment had very limited knowledge of my early childhood, which I felt was an important limitation when assessing a lifelong neurodevelopmental condition.

The assessment ultimately concluded that I was not autistic. I completely accept that an assessment does not have to result in the diagnosis someone believes they have. My concern is with the reasoning behind the conclusion and how the information I provided was interpreted.

A significant amount of my presentation was attributed to trauma. While I acknowledge that trauma can have a profound impact on someone, I had explained in detail that many of the traits I was describing had been present throughout my life and predated the traumatic experiences being discussed. I therefore felt that the possibility of autism was not adequately explored and that trauma was given too much explanatory weight.

I subsequently submitted a detailed response challenging the conclusions and requesting a senior clinical review. This is where my experience became particularly frustrating. Rather than feeling that my concerns were genuinely considered, I felt that I was effectively shut down almost immediately. I had taken the time to carefully explain why I disagreed with the conclusions and raised specific concerns about the assessment, yet I did not feel that there was a meaningful opportunity to have those concerns properly reviewed.

This was not because I simply disliked the outcome. I understood from the outset that an assessment might conclude that I was not autistic. My concern was that, having raised substantive questions about the assessment itself, I expected those questions to be taken seriously and addressed.

The whole experience has been extremely upsetting. Seeking an autism assessment is not something I took lightly, and I expected to feel that I had been given a fair, comprehensive assessment even if the eventual conclusion was not the one I hoped for.

I appreciate that autism assessments are complex and that clinicians will not always agree. However, based on my own experience, I was left feeling that important evidence and context had not been given the consideration I believe they deserved, and that when I challenged the conclusions, I was not given the opportunity for the meaningful clinical review I had hoped for.

I hope Clinical Partners takes feedback like this seriously, particularly when assessing adults whose childhood evidence may be limited and whose presentation may be complicated by masking, compensation and previous trauma.

Unfortunately, based on my experience, I would not recommend Clinical Partners for an autism assessment.

------

Edit (02/10/26): I have since sought a second opinion with another company and they took everything in to consideration, did a thorough assessment and concluded I am in fact autistic. So to those who get misdiagnosed but know they do fit the relevant framework, do your research and seek a second opinion from a far more reputable company. The Dr I had was absolutely amazing and I can't thank her enough!

The clinician did not show up to my appointment. I joined the meeting link at the scheduled time and waited for over 30 minutes. When it became clear the clinician was not going to arrive, I attempted to call the support helpline, but the lines were closed.

From the outset we were clear what we wanted - someone to manage our daughter's care, her medication & oversee/direct what therapy she might need. We were told she would need an assessment initially & were allocated a psychiatrist. In order for the appointment to proceed we had disengage from the NHS metal health team services. Post the review we were then told that the psychiatrist doesn't do medication .... so we paid for a review with someone who couldn't meet our needs and find ourselves in a place with nobody managing my daughter's medication - what a con

My experience with M&R Autos in Basingstoke has left me disappointed and questioning the service I received.

Last month, I took my car to them for a service and MOT. They do not perform MOTs on-site, so the vehicle was taken to another garage. I was charged the MOT fee plus an additional arrangement fee.

Recently, I returned because of an oil leak and smoke coming from the exhaust. I specifically asked them to identify the root cause and explained that I had recently replaced a failed turbo. However, they inspected the exhaust and catalytic converter, found oil inside the catalytic converter, and recommended replacing it. This did not address my main concern: whether there was still an active oil leak causing the problem.

I offered to supply a compatible catalytic converter from GSF Car Parts at around half the price they had quoted for the part, but they refused. Ultimately, I paid to be told what I already knew—that oil had accumulated in the exhaust system or catalytic converter—without receiving a clear diagnosis of what caused it or confirmation that the original fault had been resolved.

I also found the owner’s manner rather rude. Based on my experience, I will not be returning and cannot recommend this garage.

Update: Shortly after I posted my review, several new positive reviews appeared within a hour or 2. I cannot verify who posted them, but I found the timing unusual and now I also doubt the integrity of this garage.  I believe most of the positive reviews are posted by them only not by real customers. Well I wish the owner all the best as I do not want to harm his business , I just wanted to bring it to the public attention that i believed them based on google reviews only but they turn out to be not good.

Thank you for your response to my comments and I agree sometimes things can go wrong although isn't that why we use professional removers prevent this. If they do go wrong isn't it responsible for the removers to sort it all out?
However, your Company's lack of care and professionalism  resulting in damage to cherished possessions, some of which were beyond repair cannot be termed 'things  sometimes going wrong'. Particularly insulting was the extensive use of our  screwed up clothes, some quite expensive, to act as packing sometimes around, at the time fresh food,  this,cannot, by any stretch of anyone's imagination be called 'things going wrong.'
Your lack of interest after the event, promptly passing us to your insurers who's only interest was to refute our claim just added to the insult. I fail to see how Hackworthy can pass this off as 'sometimes things go wrong.' This comment only reinforces the lack of responsibility your Company takes in it's work.

We used Hackworthy to store our possessions for 18 months prior to a move to a new house.They collected and delivered all our stored possessions. On delivery of our possessions to our new house we found numerous items, including cherished heirlooms broken or damaged due to insufficient packing.  We found items of furniture with damage due to lack of care when moving. We found our clothes used as packing on other items. We even found fresh food packed with our clothes including mushrooms, the smell after 18 months was dreadful, the clothes around them had to be destroyed.
Our complaints to Hackworthy were met with indifference and we were advised to speak to their insurers. After many months of trying to get compensation for their failures we were offered  settlement of 50 %  of our very reasonable claim. Only on threat by us of legal action was our claim settled in full over a year after the whole fiasco started. These comments truthfully record the sorry state we were left in by Hackworthy. They are a disgrace to the removal profession.

one_star_reviews.text:
⭐ 1 star. £2,100 a month for an authentic medieval living experience.

I rented a flat managed by Cluttons from January 2024. The experience gave me a new appreciation for some of civilisation’s greatest achievements: locks, insulation, central heating, hot running water and the reply button on an email.

Within my first week, Cluttons had apparently failed to collect the previous tenant’s keys, resulting in her unlocking our front door while I was getting out of the shower. Thankfully she was lovely; unfortunately, she was greeted by me in a towel holding a kitchen knife because I assumed someone was breaking in. Nothing says “welcome home” like discovering the keys are apparently a communal free-for-all.

Then came severe damp and mould. Condensation literally ran down the walls, paint came off, paintings were damaged and we regularly discovered mould behind furniture. We reported it repeatedly. It was never properly resolved. The mould, unlike us, seemed extremely happy with the accommodation.

The real highlight was being left without heating for approximately five to six weeks during cold weather. We slept in winter coats. Inside. In London. For £2,100 a month. We also had no functioning hot water, so we boiled saucepans to wash ourselves or showered at work. No temporary heaters, alternative accommodation or compensation.

Apparently Cluttons believes heating can be replaced with wool sweaters and willpower.

I am Argentinian and even I found the property management impressively incompetent. Argentina can manage a boiler issue through WhatsApp. Cluttons had six weeks and still left us with a saucepan.

Our property managers also seemed perpetually on leave. I don’t know how much annual leave Cluttons provides, but their benefits package must be extraordinary. Eventually I found one manager’s manager online and contacted them. Miraculously, I received a reply the next day. Find someone’s manager and suddenly the ravens arrive.

Leaving was equally efficient. Cluttons only confirmed our notice had been processed about a week before moving out. Then it took four weeks to inspect the empty flat — presumably the surveyor was coming from Canterbury on foot — followed by approximately another six weeks to return our agreed deposit.

Given the medieval theme, I assume it was being delivered by mounted courier.

This wasn’t simply poor communication. We had serious damp and mould, weeks without heating or hot water, slept in winter coats and boiled saucepans to wash ourselves.

£2,100 per month. And bring your own saucepan.

And Cluttons still haven’t removed us from the building mailing list, so we continue receiving updates confirming that the communal downstairs door is still broken and being left open.

Some people get Christmas cards from their old neighbours. We get monthly confirmation that Cluttons still haven’t fixed the door.

At least they’re consistent.

One star, largely because Google won’t let me give them a saucepan.

Came to Cornwall on holiday and decided to try out a pub with good reviews nearby. The host was a delight to talk to; it's a shame the food he hyped up to be amazing was rubbish.

The special he said was delicious, and his recommendation (the Asian salmon), which I had, was completely overpriced and overcooked. My mother ordered a steak which, although tasty and cooked very well, was accompanied by the completely incorrect sides. She ordered a Greek salad with no chips but instead received a mushroom and tomato mess with chips, even though the waiter said she would be getting extra Greek salad. The supposed "Wagyu burger" was the size of a McDonald's Saver hamburger and came with maybe a child's handful of chips.

I also believe the spirits are overpriced, as other village pubs I've been to only charge around £4.50 for a single.

The best qualities of this place are definitely the venue, atmosphere, and the service. If the food were better, it would be a very nice establishment. Would have given more stars for service if the order wasn't wrong.

Edit to your response: I am not sure why you think lieing is appropriate, this review is to help other tourists not make the same mistake. My mum hates mushrooms and tomatoes so I don't know how she cleared her plate (she didn't) and we said your steak was good in the review. Without going into too much detail as this would provide a good hour of bedtime reading, my sisters phone has been out of action for 6 weeks now and still Sparta Telecom have not resolved it.

In normal situations this would be viewed as totally unacceptable, but add in that the phone is the only lifeline for my partially-sighted sister who has mobility issues  suffers from Diabetes type 2 and angina, has care workers in daily, fall sensors in place and lives in a warden aided bungalow then this long-running situation is beyond belief.

Constant broken promises, feeble daily apologies that have no substance, unreturned calls(the last being today from a manager who only yesterday informed me that Openreach would come today and not leave until it was dealt with). No call today from the manager and when calling round to see my sister tonight, suggested no engineer had even called today!

Over the last 6 weeks, Openreach to their credit have visited many times and replaced the local equipment 4 times without success. Most outcomes from the visit has requested Sparta Telecom to contact Talk Talk as the fault lies potentially at the Telephone exchange, however Sparta continue to get Openreach to go out to my sisters home instead of trying to sort out the route of the issue! Until 2 days ago I couldn't understand why Sparta kept ignoring Openreachs advice but luckily the manager at Sparta let it slip that getting Openreach out does not cost them anything but if they have to involve Talk Talk then they get charged! So, 6 weeks on and my sister who depends on the phone to arrange transport to go to her bingo club twice a week, chuch on Sundays and my phone call every day to check in that she's OK and organise her provisions, Sparta have refused to get her phone line fixed because they don't want to pay for it, even if the cost of a vulnerable lady's welfare is put at stake each and every day! This company has no empathy, deliver complaints off corporate scripts, fail to observe when requesting a priority response many times even though this us something they promote, fail to call back when promising to do so (senior manager), failing to provide written evidence of any reporting to Talk Talk and failure to temporarily cancel my sisters monthly service charge payment even though she has no phone to use! My question to Sparta is what will it take to get this phone line repaired? My sister having a fall and being left there until the carers or I turn up, without having a phone to call someone?  Currently waiting to call them again first thing tomorrow for another rant but for anyone considering going with these pirates...sail past and find a company with just an ounce or more of compassion, expertise, technical ability and customer care.

Do you literally want your customers walking around your shop on their knees?. Here's an idea, instead of putting a sign on low beams, try covering it up with some padding instead. Your obviously aware it's a problem with low beams in your shop.

You think sticking a sign on your low door beam's covers you legally?, well it doesn't.

Here's a snippet from the internet for you... " A "Mind Your Head" sign helps fulfill legal warning duties, but it does not completely remove your legal liability if someone gets hurt.

Legal Obligations and Signs fulfilling duties: Under the Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations 1996 and the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974, employers and property owners must use warning signs to highlight unavoidable hazards.

Compliance: A standard sign must follow BS EN ISO 7010 with a yellow triangle and clear symbols or text.

Why a Sign Is Not Enough

Duty of care: Courts expect you to fix or reduce risks whenever possible, not just post a warning.

Negligence: If a low ceiling or obstruction can be padded, redesigned, or blocked off, leaving it dangerous while relying only on a sticker may still count as negligence.

Visibility: A sign fails to protect you legally if it is hidden in the dark, dirty, too small, or placed too late for a person to react."

one_star_reviews.text:
We visited Ludgate Gallery in Sidmouth and were very disappointed by the way we were treated.

My daughter noticed the animal statues in the shop window and, while standing outside, touched the window to look at them. A man working inside came to the door and said, sarcastically, “Great, there’s now marks on the freshly washed windows.”

We completely understand that the windows had just been cleaned and that the shop owner may not want people touching the glass. However, there was absolutely no need to speak to us in that way. A simple, polite “please don’t touch the window” would have been perfectly reasonable.

Instead, the comment was made in a way that left my daughter and all of us feeling embarrassed and upset. Children are naturally going to be interested in animal figures displayed in a shop window, and we certainly weren’t deliberately causing any damage or being disrespectful.

For us, this really was a case of how you speak to people. It left us feeling very unwelcome and has completely put us off returning. This is a shop that relies on members of the public choosing to visit and spend their money there, so I would expect a much more courteous approach to customers and families.

one_star_reviews.text:
Completely agree with previous comments regarding accountability.

I was referred here as an NHS patient from the QEII as I need a series of operations on my hips to treat a disability. One Hatfield informed me they were unable to treat me as the operations fall outside of their specialism and would ask my GP to refer me on to a more specialist hospital.

Had this happened, I would have no cause to complain. Instead, it took nearly a month for this referral letter to be produced and shared with my GP. This is despite constant calls and chasing, explicitly informing the hospital that my GP could not do anything until they received the letter and they were actively preventing me from receiving treatment for my disability.

After nearly a month of chasing, I put in a formal complaint. This was also not acknowledged within the timeframe set out in One Hatfield's complaint policy. It was only when I told them if I didn't get a response within 24 hours that I would be escalating this further that I got a response to my complaint and my paperwork.

There has been no real investigation into why my medical notes were not shared within the 7 days that is expected by the NHS. Instead the hospital considers the matter closed because it eventually produced the documents nearly a month later.

Appalling service, negligent to their patients and a complete lack of accountability.

one_star_reviews.text:
I live immediately beside The Hub and, after months of trying to resolve concerns directly and formally with SWAY, I feel it is important to share my experience. I want to be clear that I am not against youth provision, have never asked for The Hub to close and recognise that SWAY does positive work for some young people and families.

Unfortunately, my experience as an immediate neighbour has been very different.

The Hub sits directly beside residential homes and looks towards my home and my family's private living space. Noise, doors, alarms, events, people gathering outside, parking and conversations are therefore happening immediately beside where we live.

I have raised concerns about noise, privacy, use of residential areas, safeguarding, governance, DBS and risk assessment arrangements, confidentiality and whether policies are being followed in practice. I have attended meetings, provided evidence and repeatedly suggested practical solutions and compromises.

Despite this, the Chair of Trustees recently wrote that I have “seemingly opposed nearly all” SWAY has done while “others are embracing it”. I find this deeply unfair. There is a difference between opposing an organisation and holding it accountable for matters affecting your home and family.

Some of my concerns go beyond ordinary neighbour disputes and involve safeguarding and governance questions. SWAY's initial response itself acknowledged that it was “in no way a response to every point and issue raised”. After I identified what remained unanswered, the Trustees held an extraordinary meeting and subsequently stated that they “do not consider it necessary to continue the conversation along the detailed lines” I had set out.

That has left me with very little confidence in the internal complaints process.

The situation has also become increasingly personal. I openly contacted Environmental Health about matters I believed fell within their remit. Since then, its involvement has been referred to in communications with others. I have also personally overheard a conversation outside my home in which fears were expressed that The Hub could potentially close because of matters I had escalated to authorities.

I strongly object to being made to feel responsible for the potential consequences of independent scrutiny. I can report concerns and provide evidence. I cannot determine what Environmental Health, safeguarding authorities or regulators subsequently decide.

If everything is being handled correctly, independent scrutiny should establish that. If something requiring action is identified, the person reporting it did not create the underlying issue.

SWAY publicly identifies itself as a Christian organisation. I would never judge anybody's personal faith, but unfortunately I have struggled to reconcile my experience with the values of honesty, humility, compassion, accountability, fairness and love of neighbour that I would associate with that identity. Legitimate concerns should not become personal simply because somebody continues asking for answers.

I recognise SWAY may provide genuine benefits to others. Both things can be true. An organisation can do good work while still getting individual things wrong.

After months of meetings, correspondence, evidence, suggested solutions and formal complaints, I now consider the internal process exhausted. Relevant matters will be provided to appropriate external bodies so they can reach their own conclusions.

I genuinely wish my experience had been different. I have never wanted The Hub to close. I simply believe that operating a busy youth and community facility immediately beside people's homes also brings responsibilities towards those neighbours.

Our homes, privacy, children and right to raise concerns matter too.

Being a good neighbour is not simply about believing you are one. It is also about how you treat the people living immediately beside you when they tell you something is wrong.

one_star_reviews.text:
Robbie Roskell has no involvement with this practice.  He sold it over two years ago.  In spite of this, the new owner marketed the practice as being owned and led by Robbie until very recently.  We approached RRABC in May 2025 via their website because Robbie Roskell had been recommended to us.

Lead architect and new team member, Matt Spencer-Smith, plagiarised plans drawn for a previous application but failed to adapt them.  Among other things, he confused a bathroom with a utility room, moved doors and windows and drew a staircase where there wasn’t one.  He ignored our instructions for where we wanted our new bathroom, siting it in a windowless room with no access to drainage.  When we complained, he asked us to correct his drawings with a red pen and send them back.

Crucially, Matt Spencer-Smith failed to pass information we gave him at this initial site visit about an historic bat roost to the new planning consultant, Robin Moxon.  Although Matt Spencer-Smith wrote to us soon after his visit saying he would contact Dorset Natural Environment Team about the bats, we have now learned that he didn’t do this.  Robin Moxon also failed to register information about bats when it was sent to him in writing by both Dorset Council and by ourselves.  He claims he couldn’t have known about it because it “the relevant biodiversity documentation was not publicly available on the Council planning portal”, ie it was not part of the planning application they had lifted the plans from.
No-one at RRABC  seems to have realised that the proposed works would affect a boundary wall and that this would require our neighbours’ consent.  This was another reason why the initial application was deemed invalid.

Our application was ultimately refused because RRABC failed to address the issue about the bat roost and failed to include ‘essential information’ about historic fabric in the Heritage Statement.  Robin Moxon told us he they weren’t asked for this “additional information” but it was quite clearly given as a requirement in both the Pre-Application report prepared by a Senior Conservation Officer and in Dorset Council’s “Heritage Statement Guidance and Template”.  The planning officer advised that the application be withdrawn and the plans amended but RRABC went ahead with the submission knowing it would be refused.  In the Decision Notice Dorset Council states “The applicant was offered the opportunity to submit amended plans to overcome concerns identified by the case officer but chose not to do so”

Fifteen months after our initial approach to Robbie Roskell Architectural and Building Services, we don’t have planning permission or listed building consent and RRABC has a lot of our money.

The new owner, director and team leader, Joseph Bvumburai, is a 69 year old Yorkshireman who grew up in Zambia, and now lives and works in Hull.  According to his LinkedIn profile he likes to “buy and invest in established businesses”.  Ironically he boasts about having changed his surname to “Brown” early in his career as he felt it would increase his chances of being invited for job interviews.

When we submitted a complaint to RRABC they replied that “The services contracted for were provided.”  With regard to the false details on the website, they stated that if we had wanted to know who really owned the practice, this information was “publicly available through Companies House”.

RRABC are currently marketing their services under a new website building-regs.co.uk.  They offer a pamphlet entitled “7 Hidden Issues that could delay your building project”.

⭐ 1 star – Extremely disappointing quality and after-sales service
We inherited these timber windows when we purchased the property in 2023. They had been installed approximately six years ago by Timber Windows Hereford, and the previous owners had already been trying unsuccessfully to get the problems resolved.
Unfortunately, despite continuing to raise the matter ourselves, we have experienced the same lack of satisfactory resolution.
The coating has been peeling and failing for around four years, with the deterioration continuing over time. This is not an isolated cosmetic defect affecting one window — the problems are widespread, and we have extensive photographic evidence documenting the condition.
There were also two attempts to repair the windows, but in our experience these did not resolve the problem and actually left some areas worse than they were before.
What is particularly concerning is what was stated in writing by the factory manager in correspondence dated October 2023 regarding the condition of the windows and the proposed remedial work.
The correspondence refers specifically to “blackening of the timber due to the moisture ingress” and explains that the affected areas may need to be bleached before further treatment.
Most significantly, it states:
“Due to the finish / colour of the original product, it will be difficult to achieve a perfect match / finish on the repair works.”
We find this particularly concerning. The company's own factory manager was acknowledging both moisture ingress affecting the timber and that achieving a proper finish following remedial work would be difficult.
This was therefore not simply a matter of a little routine maintenance or an isolated touch-up. We were dealing with deteriorating timber and a coating that had already been failing for years.
After repeated attempts to resolve the matter, we eventually sought independent legal advice. We were advised that we appeared to have a strong case, but after considering the cost of pursuing proceedings and the uncertainty of the outcome, we decided not to proceed with legal action.
That decision was a practical one based on the financial risk involved. It did not mean the problem had been resolved or that we were satisfied with the windows.
What is particularly frustrating is that the previous owners had already tried to resolve the problems before we purchased the property, and we have subsequently spent considerable time trying to achieve the same thing ourselves.
For what is a significant investment in timber windows, we expected considerably better durability, workmanship and after-sales support. Instead, we have been left with peeling coatings, deteriorating timber, acknowledged moisture ingress and no satisfactory long-term resolution.
The fact that the factory manager's own correspondence states that it would be “difficult to achieve a perfect match / finish” following repair is, in our view, extremely disappointing.
Anyone considering these windows should carefully investigate not only the appearance and finish when new, but also how the timber and coating perform several years down the line, what the warranty actually covers, and how problems are dealt with when they arise.
After our experience, we would not choose Timber Windows Hereford again and cannot recommend them.

Absolutely appalling customer service

I chose Randox because I assumed a company specialising in health testing would be professional, organised and capable of tracking a biological sample. Apparently, that was too much to expect.

I sent my sample last Tuesday. It is now Monday and, after calling customer service on Friday and again today, they still cannot even tell me whether my sample has reached the laboratory. Not when I will get my results. Not whether there is a delay. They cannot even tell me if they have my sample.

The website says results can take up to 7 working days *from receipt of the sample*. Fine. But apparently there is no way for the customer to know when that clock actually starts.

Their solution? I was told I should have taken a photo of the Royal Mail tracking information. Except nowhere in the instructions I was given did it clearly say that I needed to do this. I followed their instructions carefully, kept my URN, and somehow I am now expected to have anticipated that Randox's own tracking system is so useless that I need to create my own evidence that I posted the sample.

The website, FAQ and instructions are confusing and poorly designed, there is no proper sample tracking or status update system, email enquiries are apparently ignored, and the phone support is so poorly equipped that on multiple occasions they couldn't even locate or provide meaningful information about my test.

This is a health testing company. You are dealing with samples that people have paid to have analysed, often for matters that are already stressful and personal. The absolute minimum you should provide is a basic system allowing customers to know that their sample has arrived and is being processed.

Instead, the entire experience feels like: send your sample into the void and hope someone eventually finds it.

Extremely disappointing. I would not recommend Randox for home testing based on this experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
My experience of Harcourt Chambers, and in particular the handling of my family case by Elisabeth Wickham, has left me profoundly dissatisfied with the standard of service I received and with Chambers' subsequent handling of my complaint.

This was a final hearing concerning my children, where accuracy, careful communication of instructions and precise drafting were exceptionally important. My concerns are not simply that I disliked the outcome. They concern the way my instructions were handled, the move from an anticipated evidential hearing to determination on submissions, what happened when I subsequently gave an urgent written instruction before judgment, and significant problems I say arose in translating the outcome into the final order.

I made a detailed formal complaint. It was determined by Professor Rob George KC. While his determination rejected most of my complaints, it did make an important finding concerning the drafting process: an unresolved issue concerning the parenting app was effectively removed from the Judge's consideration, and Professor George KC concluded that it would have been better for the disputed wording to remain before the Judge for adjudication.

I was particularly disappointed, however, by the wider approach to disputed evidence. In my view, considerable weight was placed on EW's later recollection of oral discussions when determining what I had supposedly understood, agreed and subsequently instructed. I do not believe sufficient weight was given to the significance of contemporaneous written communications and the overall pattern of events. I found it particularly troubling that matters such as my not openly contradicting my own barrister in court, and even the fact that I gave my barrister and solicitor a lift to the station after the hearing without complaining during the journey, featured in the assessment. In my view, remaining civil towards one's legal representatives is very poor evidence of satisfaction with their professional service.

The consequences were not merely academic. Subsequent implementation of the final order generated disputes about its wording, correspondence seeking clarification, allegations of breach and threatened enforcement. The mother's solicitors ultimately agreed temporary holiday handover times materially different from the strict times they had previously sought to enforce. In my view, that subsequent history is difficult to reconcile with treating the drafting concerns as merely insignificant.

I have now asked Harcourt Chambers to review/reconsider the complaint determination and supplied further contemporaneous evidence, including communications from the hearing itself. I will update this review fairly when that process is concluded.

For anyone considering instructing Chambers, my experience has left me with serious concerns about attention to detail, preservation and communication of client instructions, drafting precision, and how Chambers investigates a complaint when the client's account conflicts with counsel's subsequent recollection.

Given the importance and cost of family proceedings, I expected considerably better.

one_star_reviews.text:
This review relates specifically to Oxford Health NHS Foundation Trust’s PALS/Complaints service based at the Whiteleaf Centre, not to the clinical services at Whiteleaf generally.

I am concerned about the accuracy of information provided by this service and the potential wider impact on Buckinghamshire patients seeking independent NHS complaints advocacy.

On three separate occasions, across two formal complaints, I was directed by Oxford Health PALS/Complaints staff to VoiceAbility for NHS complaints advocacy in Buckinghamshire.

The first documented occasion was 9 September 2025. The same information was then provided again on 7 June 2026 and 9 June 2026, including by service-lead level staff.

On 17 August 2026, VoiceAbility confirmed to me that it is not the locally commissioned NHS complaints advocacy provider for Buckinghamshire and that the correct provider is The Advocacy People.

Oxford Health subsequently acknowledged in writing that the Buckinghamshire information had been overwritten with Oxfordshire information, including details of the Oxfordshire advocacy service. Oxford Health also confirmed that the Buckinghamshire template was corrected after I raised the issue.

The same incorrect advocacy information was therefore provided to me across two complaints over a documented period of approximately 11 months.

The practical impact on me was significant. I contacted VoiceAbility on 10 June 2026 after being directed there by Oxford Health. I was not informed until 17 August 2026 that I needed to approach a different provider. This resulted in a 68-day delay before I was directed to the correct locally commissioned advocacy service.

My concern extends beyond my own case.

A VoiceAbility staff member subsequently told me that they recalled signposting “a number of Bucks clients” in the past and said Oxford Health’s signposting error “may be why”. They also said that raising the issue would help others receive the correct support more quickly in future.

I am therefore seriously concerned about how long incorrect advocacy information remained within a Buckinghamshire complaints service without being identified, and about the potential effect on other Buckinghamshire patients who may have received the same template information.

I am also concerned about the potential avoidable impact on VoiceAbility. If Buckinghamshire residents were being directed there incorrectly, VoiceAbility staff may have spent unnecessary time dealing with enquiries and redirecting people to the appropriate provider.

I have raised these concerns with VoiceAbility’s management/feedback team so they can consider any wider impact on their service. I have also raised the matter with relevant external oversight and regulatory bodies so that the potential wider public-interest implications can be considered independently.

Given that Oxford Health has confirmed that the problem was within the Buckinghamshire template itself, and that I received the same incorrect information over approximately 11 months, I believe it is reasonable to question how widely that template may have been used and whether other complainants were affected.

I welcome the fact that Oxford Health acknowledged the error and corrected the template once I raised it. However, that does not remove the 68-day delay I experienced or my concern about the potential wider impact while the incorrect information was in use.

For anyone in Buckinghamshire who needs independent NHS complaints advocacy, VoiceAbility confirmed to me that the correct locally commissioned provider is The Advocacy People. Their contact details can be found through The Advocacy People’s official website.

For these reasons, my experience of the PALS/Complaints service has been very poor.
